paper_title: RLHF Workflow From Reward Modeling to Online RLHF
caption: The training record of reward modeling. From the left to right, we present the records of training loss, gradient norm, and the learning rate, respectively.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how the gradient norm of a reward model changes over training, showing a single time-series trace labeled in the legend as “Gradient Norm of Reward Model.” The x-axis is labeled “Training Step,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 7000 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, and 7000. The y-axis is labeled “Gradient Norm,” uses a linear scale, and displays values roughly from 5 up to 40 with major tick labels at intervals of 5 (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40). A single blue solid line (no markers) starts near a gradient norm of about 40 at training step 0, drops steeply within the early steps to below 10, and then continues with small fluctuations mostly between about 5 and 8 across the remainder of training; it includes occasional narrow upward spikes (for example, around steps near ~2900 reaching a bit above 10 and near ~4100 reaching roughly the low-to-mid teens), after which it returns to the baseline fluctuation band, and it ends near training steps around 6800–7000 at approximately 7.
